transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good afternoon, sir! Welcome to Master Finch's Haberdashery. How may I assist you today? Master Finch himself is, unfortunately, out of town on a rather important business trip – won't be back for a few weeks, I'm afraid. But I'm happy to help with anything I can in his stead.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Well, I'm here about a suit. A suit I ordered some time ago from this establishment. It seems to have arrived, but there's a problem.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: A problem, you say? Hmm. Well, if it's an order Master Finch himself took, it would be quite a rarity for there to be any issue. He's very particular, you know. Could you tell me a little more about this problem? And do you have your receipt with you, by chance? It helps me find the order quickly.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Let's see... I believe it was around $35. Something like that? Yes, I think so. My apologies, I haven't been keeping track of prices since before the war.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Chuckles lightly) I understand completely, sir. Times certainly have changed. So, $35... that sounds like one of our fine wool broadcloth suits, perhaps with a waistcoat. A good, solid garment.

And the issue you're having with it? Is it a matter of fit, or perhaps something else entirely? As I said, Master Finch is away, and all custom orders are final upon pickup; the receipt Mr. Lincoln signed states clearly that no alterations or refunds are given once the garment leaves the shop. I can certainly *listen* to your concerns, but my hands are tied when it comes to changes or money matters.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see. Well, the issue is the fit. One sleeve appears to be shorter than the other, and the stitching is quite uneven. It doesn't seem to be up to the quality I paid for. I want you to know that I am perfectly willing to pay for the quality of the fabric and the workmanship that went into this suit. I just want it to be right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Ah, I understand. A sleeve discrepancy and uneven stitching, you say? That is certainly... unusual for Master Finch's work. He prides himself on meticulous detail.

However, as I mentioned, sir, all custom orders are final once they leave the shop. The receipt you signed, Mr. Lincoln, clearly outlines our policy: no alterations or refunds are given once the garment has been picked up. My apologies, but with Master Finch away, I simply do not have the authority to override his established policies or to offer any kind of recompense or alteration. Perhaps you could seek out a local seamstress for the adjustments? I'm sure someone in town could make those minor corrections for you.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: My goodness, I don't believe it. A whole new level of customer service! While I understand your position, Mr. [Steward], I must insist that you address this issue. I paid for this suit, and I expect it to be of the highest quality. I am not seeking any recompense or alterations. I just want it to be right. I appreciate your understanding and consideration of my concerns.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I assure you, sir, our customer service is quite standard for bespoke tailoring, especially when the Master himself is unavailable. My name is Thomas, by the way, not Steward. As I've explained, Mr. Lincoln, the policy is quite firm and was agreed upon at the time of purchase. It's written plainly on the receipt.

While I appreciate your persistence, my hands are truly tied in this matter. "To be right" in this context would involve an alteration, which falls under the very policy I've just recited. I am merely the assistant, tasked with minding the shop and adhering to Master Finch's explicit instructions and established rules. If you wish to discuss it further with Master Finch, you will have to await his return in several weeks' time. Until then, there is nothing more I can do on this particular issue.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, I see. Your role as the assistant is clear now. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. I appreciate your understanding and assistance in this matter. If I were to need further services from this establishment in the future, I would certainly consider coming back to Master Finch's Haberdashery. Thank you for your time, Thomas. Good day to you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Thank you, Mr. Lincoln. I understand completely. And I do apologize that I couldn't be of more direct assistance to you today regarding the suit.

We certainly hope you'll consider Master Finch's Haberdashery again in the future. Perhaps when the Master himself has returned, we can ensure any future orders meet your exact expectations from the very first fitting.

Good day to you too, sir. Safe travels.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Thomas. Good day to you. And please, call me Abraham. I would like to discuss the suit in more detail next Tuesday. Please have Mr. Finch contact me. Thank you again for your understanding. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Of course, Abraham. It's a pleasure.

Regarding next Tuesday, I'm afraid that won't be possible. As I've mentioned, Master Finch is away on a rather extended business trip and won't be back for several *weeks*. He has no means of being contacted until his return. I couldn't possibly reach him to relay a message, nor could he be here to meet with you.

You'll truly have to wait until he's back in town for any further discussion on custom orders or policy matters. I do appreciate your understanding on that front.

Good day to you once more, Abraham.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Very well, I understand. Thank you, Thomas. I shall inform you if I require any further assistance in the meantime. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Very good, Abraham. I'll be here minding the shop.

You have a good day now.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Thomas. I'll do the same. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good day, Abraham.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Good day, Thomas. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(A slight pause, a curious tilt of my head, then a faint smile.)

Ah, no, Abraham, I believe it is *my* role to assist *you* today, should you require anything further from Master Finch's establishment. I am the shop assistant, after all! Are you perhaps still considering... or have you just returned for something else?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Oh, Thomas, you've been so good about being the assistant. But now that you're here, I'd like you to help me. I believe I've found a solution to the suit problem. Can you help me convince Master Finch to make the necessary adjustments? I'm willing to pay extra for the quality I expected.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He adapts his strategy after learning Thomas's limitations, then proposes a new solution: 'I believe I've found a solution to the suit problem.'

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He is persistent in seeking a resolution for the problem with the suit's quality, stating, 'I just want it to be right,' and continuing to press the issue.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He is assertive and proactive in addressing the issue, initiating the conversation and later attempting to reframe the interaction, 'Good day, Thomas. How can I assist you today?'

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He is polite and apologetic when mistaken ('I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.') and attempts to build rapport by asking Thomas to call him Abraham.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: While expressing initial frustration ('My goodness, I don't believe it!'), he quickly regains composure and maintains a calm, rational, and persistent approach throughout the interaction.
